text_blocks.snippet: Several COVID-19 variants have emerged, with some becoming more prominent than others. Notable variants include Beta, Delta, and Omicron. Beta was first identified in South Africa and was more contagious than the original strain. Delta, first found in India, was significantly more transmissible than the Alpha variant. Omicron, first identified in Botswana and South Africa, is currently driving most SARS-CoV-2 infections.
Here's a more detailed look at some of the variants:

list.title: Beta:
list.snippet: Identified in South Africa at the end of 2020, Beta was estimated to be around 50% more contagious than the original strain.

list.title: Delta:
list.snippet: First detected in India, Delta was significantly more transmissible than earlier variants, including Alpha. According to Wikipedia, it was first identified on October 5, 2020, and had spread to over 179 countries by November 2021.

list.title: Omicron:
list.snippet: First identified in Botswana and South Africa in late November 2021, Omicron subvariants are currently the dominant strains causing infections.
